transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-19
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Soto (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (CascadeLabs VP Eng), Maya Chen (SRE lead), Diego Alvarez (CTO), Ruchi Patel (Security)
Recording: auto
Shared artifacts: Incident runbook (link), sanitized telemetry request (link), proposed batching spreadsheet (link)

Summary:
A short postmortem bridgecall following last week's production cascade where long-tail token delays and fallback amplification caused higher 99th pct latency and a partial degradation of user flows. Focus was on validating mitigations Redwood pushed (prefix KV cache tuning and conservative batching), aligning on a 48-hr canary, and agreeing next steps for a potential on-prem pilot if regressions persist.

Topics covered:
- Incident timeline recap and primary signal windows
- Root cause hypotheses (KV cache thrash + aggressive batching during traffic spike)
- Validation of fixes shipped (cache TTL change, fallback gating)
- Canary design and success criteria
- Data access and security constraints for trace sharing
- Risk and rollback criteria for pilot

Action items (recapped at end):
- Jordan: provide sanitized traces + KV cache snapshot by 2025-05-22
- Priya: deliver tuned batching/caching config + runbook by 2025-05-21
- Maya: run 48-hour canary and report deviations by 2025-05-23
- Alex: draft SOW addendum and pilot scope by 2025-05-28

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the quick turn. We know it was a noisy week so we'll try to keep this tight. Jordan Kim, Redwood AE. Priya and Alex here on our side.
[00:18] Maya: Hi, Maya here, uh, on SRE. We're mostly interested in, like, whether the KV cache changes actually stopped the token amplification we saw.
[00:27] Priya: Yeah, quick correction — during the fix we adjusted the prefix K V cache TTL and also changed the continuous batching thresholds so the system doesn't pull too much into one window.
[00:40] Liam: Quick question: when you say "continuous batching" are you talking about the service-level batching or the runtime-level batching? We've got both in the stack and we need to be precise.
[00:52] Priya: Good call. I mean runtime-level batching in the Redwood inference runtime — the thing that coalesces requests per-GPU. But we also put conservative guards in the service layer to avoid over-accumulation.
[01:05] Diego: There was one point where our monitor showed fallback loops — where a downstream fallback call caused a cache eviction storm. Is that what you mean by KV thrash?
[01:16] Priya: Yep, basically the KV cache had a series of small TTLs in a few hot prefixes and when traffic spiked concurrent evictions and reloads caused bursts of long tail latency, which then triggered the fallback policy and amplified downstream load.
[01:30] Jordan: I want to stress the fallback gating change — we reduced aggressive fallback retries and added a short-debounce before a fallback executes; that reduced the immediate amplification in our tests.
[01:42] Ruchi: From security — we need sanitized traces. We can't accept raw PII in shared telemetry. What's the plan there?
[01:50] Alex: We'll put together a sanitized trace package: hashes only, remove prompt content, and provide timeline and request ids you can map to your internal logs. Jordan will send it.
[02:05] Jordan: Yep I'll share the sanitized request traces and a KV cache snapshot. We'll also include a small doc describing how we scrubbed the data.
[02:15] Liam: On the changes you shipped, did you also tweak the quan-tization profile? I recall some noise there in the release notes.
[02:24] Priya: We did not change quantization in prod for this patch; that was kept constant. There was a plan to try low-risk 8-bit profiles, but we didn't roll that out during the incident. So the hypothesis remains centered on cache + batching.
[02:40] Maya: Ok, good. Next, about the canary — we want to run something that mirrors our peak 95-99 traffic for at least 48 hours and we need clear success criteria.
[02:52] Jordan: Proposed criteria: 99th pct latency within 10% of baseline, fallback rate below 0.5% absolute, no increase in error rate. Also no sustained token-per-request delta beyond 3% — that caught some of your costs last week.
[03:11] Diego: That sounds reasonable. Can we get those thresholds in a checklist so our on-call can follow?
[03:17] Priya: We'll produce a canary runbook with metrics and alert thresholds. I'll include the exact Prometheus queries and the dashboard links.
[03:28] Liam: Re: the canary traffic — is there any warmup or priming we should be doing for the KV cache? We saw a cold start penalty last time.
[03:36] Priya: Yes, recommend a synthetic warmup sequence to prime hot prefixes for an hour before the canary window. We'll provide a minimal traffic generator script.
[03:46] Maya: Good. Also, on the subject of rollback and the pilot: if the canary shows regressions, what's the immediate rollback path you recommend?
[03:55] Jordan: If regressions exceed thresholds we'll revert batching to the previous config and re-enable the old fallback gating while we investigate. For pilot we want a safe rollback criteria in the SOW.
[04:06] Alex: I'll draft that into the SOW addendum — include rollback clauses and a decision tree.
[04:12] Ruchi: A couple of compliance notes: we need assurance on KMS key handling if telemetry includes any identifiers. Can you confirm segregation?
[04:21] Priya: All artifacts we share will be encrypted at rest and keys will stay in our KMS. For the sanitized pack we'll also provide HMACs so you can verify integrity.
[04:34] Maya: You mentioned reduced retry policy — can you quantify what you changed?
[04:39] Priya: Previously retries were 3 attempts with exponential backoff; we cut retries to 1 with a 200ms debounce on fallback evaluation, and we also added a per-prefix circuit-breaker to avoid repeated hits to the same key under duress.
[04:55] Liam: Interesting. Does that impact successful throughput? Will we drop requests?
[05:00] Priya: No, it's more conservative on retries; we prefer returning soft degradation than spinning fallback loops. Throughput remained stable in our pre/post internal tests. There is a small increase in tail error rate in pathological synthetic tests but not in realistic traffic shapes.
[05:17] Diego: I want to see the pre/post graphs. Can we get a side-by-side of 95/99/99.9 percentiles?
[05:23] Jordan: Yes — the sanitized telemetry will include percentile breakdowns and token counts. We'll also highlight the time windows you care about.
[05:33] Maya: One more operational ask: can Redwood provide an option to auto-disable batching during sudden surge events for our critical routes? We want an emergency off-ramp.
[05:42] Priya: We have a routing policy that can pin requests to a low-latency path — we can enable a per-route emergency flag so your on-call can flip it. There's also an API to change batching thresholds on the fly.
[05:55] Liam: Is there a UI toggle in the console for that or is it API only?
[06:00] Jordan: Both. We'll show the console toggle in the next demo if you want.
[06:06] Alex: Quick note — if you decide to move forward with an on-prem pilot we need to scope network egress, physical hardware, and an acceptance test. I'll draft the SOW first.
[06:18] Diego: We may prefer a VPC private deployment rather than full on-prem. Something to discuss once canary completes.
[06:25] Ruchi: Also, timeline: we have an audit next month. We need all artifact handling to be auditable.
[06:31] Jordan: Understood — we'll include an audit ledger and the sanitization checklist.
[06:37] Maya: Ok, let's go over the rough timeline. When will we get the traces?
[06:41] Jordan: I'll send the sanitized package by EOD 2025-05-22. Priya will get the runbook and config by 2025-05-21. Then you plan the canary starting 2025-05-21 or 05-22, and Maya reports by 05-23. Alex will send SOW draft by 05-28.
[06:58] Liam: Sounds good. One last thing — did you see any sign that a model change (new weights) might have contributed?
[07:06] Priya: We checked model hash across the timeframe — no changes. The models were the same, so that rules out model churn. It was infra-level interplay.
[07:16] Diego: Great. We'll queue the canary and set up an on-call for the window.
[07:22] Jordan: Thanks. We'll follow up with the secure links and the runbook.
[07:26] Alex: I'll also open a short JIRA epic with these action items and share with your PM.
[07:31] Maya: Perfect. Thanks, everyone.
[07:34] Jordan: Thanks all, adjourn.

Call end: ~15:58 UTC

Post-call notes:
- Jordan uploaded a sanitized telemetry bundle to the shared folder (link noted in chat). Maya confirmed receipt in the chat.
- Priya attached a minimal traffic generator and a canary runbook skeleton.
- Alex created CRM ticket CRM-CL-6743 and will circulate SOW draft next week.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had some mis-hearings around technical terms (e.g., "K V cache" for KV cache, "quan-tization" for quantization, and occasional name swaps). Speakers occasionally overlap in rapid clarification sections.
